papers.titleEn: Reengineering ELISA through Solid-Phase Transfer: A Wash-Free 3D Pillar-Array Immunoassay for Clothianidin Detection
papers.abstract: Accurate and field-deployable detection of clothianidin is hindered by the insufficient specificity of existing antibodies and the tedious washing procedures of conventional enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs). Herein, we addressed these limitations through innovations in both molecular recognition and assay formats. First, computer-aided modeling and animal immunization were combined to generate an ultrahigh-specificity monoclonal antibody (mAb) against clothianidin. The mAb exhibited cross-reactivity below 0.1% toward the nine neonicotinoid analogues tested, which is superior to the specificity of the previously reported clothianidin antibodies. Second, a novel three-dimensional polystyrene pillar array was developed, with coating antigens immobilized on the pillar surfaces. Sequential transfer of the array between reaction solutions enabled a “transfer instead of washing” strategy, eliminating conventional plate-washing procedures. Combined with smartphone-based colorimetric detection, the developed wash-free immunoassay showed a linear range of 1.88−60 ng/mL and a limit of detection of 0.44 ng/mL, with a total assay time of approximately 70 min. Spiked vegetable samples yielded recoveries of 88.9%−115.0% with coefficients of variation ≤12.3%, and blind sample results agreed well with the LC−MS/MS method. The pillar array can be transported in an ice box and remains stable throughout a field campaign, and the workflow requires no microplate reader or plate washer, providing a portable, laboratory-independent, and equipment-free approach for quantitative, decentralized clothianidin screening.
